title: Comparative Analysis — Vata vs. Pitta vs. Kapha Doshas
content: A comparative overview of the three doshas highlights their distinct physiological functions, elements, and attributes: 1. Elemental Makeup: Vata is Ether + Air; Pitta is Fire + Water; Kapha is Water + Earth. 2. Primary Role: Vata is Kinetic/Catabolic (movement, nerve transmission, excretion); Pitta is Metabolic/Transformative (digestion, enzymatic reactions, heat); Kapha is Structural/Anabolic (cohesion, growth, lubrication). 3. Thermal Nature: Vata is Cold (Sheeta); Pitta is Hot (Ushna); Kapha is Cold (Sheeta). 4. Moisture Nature: Vata is Dry (Ruksha); Pitta is Lightly Oily (Sasneha); Kapha is Very Oily/Unctuous (Snigdha). 5. Weight/Density: Vata is Light (Laghu); Pitta is Light (Laghu); Kapha is Heavy (Guru). 6. Primary Seat in Body: Vata resides primarily in the colon (Pakwashaya), pelvis, and bones; Pitta resides in the small intestine (Grahani), stomach, and liver; Kapha resides in the chest (Uras), throat, and head.

title: Classical Ayurveda Literature — The Brihat Trayi (Great Triad)
content: The authoritative corpus of classical Ayurveda is anchored in the 'Brihat Trayi' (The Great Three Treatises): 1. Charaka Samhita: Primarily attributed to Acharya Charaka, focusing predominantly on Kaya Chikitsa (internal medicine), foundational philosophy, epistemology, etiology (Nidana), and therapeutics. Emphasizes mind-body balance and lifestyle. 2. Sushruta Samhita: Attributed to Acharya Sushruta, known globally as the pioneer of surgery (Shalya Chikitsa); details surgical procedures, rhinoplasty, anatomical dissections (Sharira), surgical instruments, and trauma management. 3. Ashtanga Hridaya / Ashtanga Sangraha: Composed by Acharya Vagbhata; brilliantly synthesizes and condenses the core teachings of both Charaka and Sushruta into poetic, memorable Sanskrit verses covering all eight clinical branches of Ayurveda (Ashtanga Ayurveda).
source: History of Indian Medicine and AYUSH Research
section: Classical Heritage: Overview of Brihat Trayi

title: The Eight Clinical Branches — Ashtanga Ayurveda
content: Ayurveda traditionally encompasses eight specialized medical branches, termed Ashtanga Ayurveda: 1. Kaya Chikitsa: Internal medicine and general systemic disorders. 2. Shalya Tantra: Surgical techniques, wound care, and foreign body extraction. 3. Shalakya Tantra: Disorders of the ear, nose, throat, eyes, and oral cavity (supraclavicular medicine). 4. Kaumarabhritya: Pediatrics, obstetrics, and gynecology. 5. Agada Tantra: Toxicology, poisons, and environmental hazards. 6. Rasayana Tantra: Rejuvenation, geriatrics, longevity science, and cellular vitalization. 7. Vajikarana Tantra: Virility, reproductive health, and healthy progeny. 8. Bhuta Vidya (Graha Chikitsa): Psychotherapy and psycho-spiritual health. Together, these branches provided a comprehensive healthcare matrix in classical India.
source: Ministry of AYUSH — Classical Ayurvedic Frameworks
